project: Claude Code Bot - v2.1 Polish, Memory & Permissions
description: CLI improvements, Telegram hardening, persistent memory system, interactive tool permissions, and config backward compatibility

testCommands.lint: uv run ruff check src/ agent.py

userStories.title: Add extra="ignore" to BotConfig for backward compat
userStories.description: Add model_config = ConfigDict(extra='ignore') to BotConfig so old config.yaml files with removed sections (e.g. memory:) don't cause Pydantic validation errors on upgrade.
acceptanceCriteria: BotConfig has model_config = ConfigDict(extra='ignore')
Loading a config.yaml with an unknown key (e.g. memory: {}) does not raise ValidationError
Existing valid configs still load correctly
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Small change. Add a test that loads config with extra unknown fields and verifies no error.

userStories.title: Add show_tool_activity config option per channel
userStories.description: Add show_tool_activity as a channel setting in config.yaml. The Telegram channel should read this from its channel settings dict and use it to toggle tool activity display.
acceptanceCriteria: ChannelConfig settings can include show_tool_activity: true/false
TelegramChannel reads show_tool_activity from channel settings in app.py lifespan
HTTP SSE endpoint always streams tool events (client decides what to display)
Default is false if not specified
config.example.yaml updated with commented-out example
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Update app.py lifespan to pass show_tool_activity from channel settings to TelegramChannel. Add test verifying the setting is respected.

userStories.title: Add --api-key flag to CLI agent.py
userStories.description: Add --api-key flag to CLI that sends X-API-Key header with all HTTP requests, so the CLI works when the HTTP channel has api_key authentication configured.
acceptanceCriteria: New --api-key CLI argument
When provided, all requests include X-API-Key header
Health check also sends the header
Works with streaming endpoint
Help text documents the flag
userStories.notes: Pass headers dict to httpx.get and httpx.stream calls. Add test that verifies header is sent when flag is provided.

userStories.title: Add color/ANSI formatting to CLI tool indicators
userStories.description: Add ANSI color formatting to CLI output: dim gray for tool indicators, bold for bot name, and a visible separator after results.
acceptanceCriteria: Tool start/done indicators shown in dim/gray ANSI color
Error messages shown in red
Conversation switch shown in cyan
Colors disabled when stdout is not a TTY (piped output)
No external color library dependency — use raw ANSI codes
userStories.notes: Use sys.stdout.isatty() check. Define ANSI constants (DIM, RED, CYAN, RESET). Wrap existing print calls.

userStories.title: Persist conversation_id in CLI interactive mode
userStories.description: In interactive mode, capture the conversation_id from the first streamed result event and reuse it for all subsequent messages in the same session, so the conversation stays consistent without needing the --conversation flag.
acceptanceCriteria: First message response's session_id/conversation_id is captured
Subsequent messages in the same interactive session automatically use that conversation_id
--conversation flag still overrides if provided
Conversation ID shown on connect when auto-detected
userStories.notes: The SSE result event already includes session_id. Need to also return conversation_id from the SSE endpoint. Update send_streaming to return the conversation_id, then persist it in the interactive loop.

userStories.title: Split long Telegram responses into multiple messages
userStories.description: Telegram has a 4096 character limit per message. Split long agent responses into multiple messages, breaking at paragraph or sentence boundaries when possible.
acceptanceCriteria: Responses over 4096 chars split into multiple Telegram messages
Split prefers paragraph boundaries (double newline), then single newline, then space
Each chunk is <= 4096 characters
Messages sent in order with short delay between them
Short responses (<= 4096) sent as single message (no behavior change)
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Add a _split_message(text, max_len=4096) helper. Test with strings of various lengths and break patterns.

userStories.title: Add retry on connection drop during CLI streaming
userStories.description: If the SSE connection drops mid-stream, retry the request. Show the partial text received so far and indicate a retry is happening.
acceptanceCriteria: On httpx.ReadError or httpx.RemoteProtocolError during streaming, retry up to 2 times
Partial text already displayed is not re-displayed
User sees a [Reconnecting...] indicator
If all retries fail, show error message
Works in both single-message and interactive mode
userStories.notes: Wrap the streaming loop in a retry. Since text is printed as it arrives, partial output is already visible. On retry, the server starts fresh so there may be duplicate content — acceptable tradeoff.

userStories.title: Add thinking indicator for long Telegram agent runs
userStories.description: For agent runs that take longer than a threshold, send a 'thinking...' message that gets edited with the final response, instead of relying solely on the typing indicator which may expire.
acceptanceCriteria: If agent processing exceeds 10 seconds, a 'Thinking...' message is sent
When the response is ready, the thinking message is edited with the final text
If response is fast (< 10s), no thinking message — behaves as before
Thinking threshold is configurable via channel settings (default 10s)
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Use asyncio.create_task with a sleep(threshold) that sends the thinking message. Cancel it if the response arrives first. If thinking was sent, use message.edit_text() instead of message.answer().

userStories.title: Add persistent memory system with folder structure
userStories.description: Create a memory system at ~/.claude-bot/memory/ with three zones: core/ (read-only for bot, manually curated by owner), to_improve/ (bot writes self-improvement suggestions), and the rest of the folder where the bot freely organizes its own notes and knowledge. The memory contents are loaded into the system prompt context. Add MemoryStore class to manage reading/writing.
acceptanceCriteria: New src/claude_code_bot/memory_store.py with MemoryStore class
MemoryStore.memory_path configurable via config.yaml (default ~/.claude-bot/memory/)
Auto-creates ~/.claude-bot/memory/, ~/.claude-bot/memory/core/, ~/.claude-bot/memory/to_improve/ on startup
MemoryStore.load_core() reads all files in core/ recursively and returns combined text
MemoryStore.load_all() reads core/ + to_improve/ + any other files/folders the bot created
MemoryStore.write(path, content) writes to memory folder — REFUSES to write to core/ (raises PermissionError)
MemoryStore.delete(path) deletes from memory folder — REFUSES to delete from core/
MemoryStore.list(subfolder=None) lists files in memory or subfolder
Path traversal protection — no writing outside memory_path
Memory content injected into system prompt by AgentService._build_system_prompt()

Memory section in system prompt formatted as: '## Memory
### Core
{core_content}
### Notes
{other_content}'
Typecheck passes
Tests cover: read core, write to_improve, write custom folder, refuse write to core, refuse path traversal, auto-create dirs
userStories.notes: Use pathlib for all path operations. The memory_path in config should expand ~ via Path.expanduser(). Docker-compose should mount a host volume to ~/.claude-bot/memory/. MemoryStore is initialized in app.py lifespan and passed to AgentService.

userStories.title: Add memory MCP tools for agent self-management
userStories.description: Create MCP tools that let the agent read, write, list, and delete files in its memory folder. The agent uses these tools via natural language (e.g. 'save this for later', 'what do you remember about X'). Core folder is read-only.
acceptanceCriteria: New MCP tools in src/claude_code_bot/memory_tools.py: memory_read, memory_write, memory_list, memory_delete
memory_read(path) reads a file from memory, works on all zones including core/
memory_write(path, content) writes to memory — returns error if path starts with core/
memory_list(subfolder?) lists files in memory root or subfolder
memory_delete(path) deletes file — returns error if path starts with core/
Tools registered as MCP server and added to allowed_tools in agent options
Agent system prompt includes instruction about memory tools usage
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Uses @tool decorator + create_sdk_mcp_server(). NOTE: MCP tools with query() had a ProcessTransport bug in SDK v0.1.26. This story should use ClaudeSDKClient instead of query() if the bug persists. Test by checking if MCP tools work first. If SDK bug still exists, mark this story as blocked and add a note — the MemoryStore from US-209 still works via system prompt injection as a fallback.

userStories.title: Update system prompt with memory instructions
userStories.description: Update the default system prompt and config.example.yaml with clear instructions for the bot about how to use its memory system. Also update Aristo's config.yaml system prompt.
acceptanceCriteria: config.example.yaml system_prompt includes memory instructions
Memory instructions explain: core/ is read-only (owner-curated), to_improve/ is for self-improvement suggestions, rest of memory/ is bot-managed
Instructions tell bot to proactively save important context, user preferences, and recurring topics
Instructions tell bot to organize its own notes with meaningful folder/file names
Instructions tell bot to check memory at start of conversations for relevant context
AgentService._build_system_prompt() appends memory content AFTER the persona system prompt
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: The system prompt memory section is auto-injected by _build_system_prompt(), so the config.yaml system_prompt just needs behavioral instructions, not the actual memory content. Suggest updating Aristo's system_prompt to replace the informal memory instructions with the standardized ones.

userStories.title: Add permission_mode and allowed_tools to config
userStories.description: Add SDK permission configuration to config.yaml: permission_mode (default 'acceptEdits'), allowed_tools list, and disallowed_tools list. These are passed to ClaudeAgentOptions.
acceptanceCriteria: New fields in BotConfig: permission_mode (str, default 'acceptEdits'), allowed_tools (list[str], default []), disallowed_tools (list[str], default [])
Values passed to ClaudeAgentOptions in AgentService.chat_stream()
config.example.yaml updated with documented defaults and examples
If allowed_tools is empty, no restriction (SDK default)
permission_mode validates against known values: default, acceptEdits, plan, bypassPermissions
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Simple config-to-options passthrough. Add tests that verify the options are correctly built from config values.

userStories.title: Add interactive tool permission via can_use_tool callback
userStories.description: Implement a can_use_tool callback that asks users for permission via their channel (HTTP or Telegram) when the agent wants to use a dangerous tool. Uses asyncio.Event to wait for user response. Configurable list of tools that require approval.
acceptanceCriteria: New src/claude_code_bot/permissions.py with PermissionManager class
PermissionManager.request_permission(user_id, tool_name, input_data, channel) sends permission request to user's active channel
HTTP channel: emits SSE event {type: 'permission_request', tool: str, input_summary: str, request_id: str} — client responds via POST /permissions/{request_id} with {approved: bool}
Telegram channel: sends inline keyboard message 'Allow [tool_name]? [Yes] [No]' — callback query handler processes response
PermissionManager waits up to 60s for user response (configurable timeout), default deny on timeout
New config field: tools_requiring_approval (list[str], default ['Bash']) — tools that trigger interactive permission
can_use_tool callback created by PermissionManager and passed to ClaudeAgentOptions
Tools NOT in the approval list are auto-allowed per the permission_mode setting
Permission request includes a human-readable summary of what the tool wants to do (e.g. 'Run command: ls -la')
POST /permissions/{request_id} endpoint added to app.py
Telegram callback query handler added to telegram.py
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: This is the most complex story. Key design: PermissionManager holds a dict of pending requests (request_id -> asyncio.Event + result). The can_use_tool callback creates a request, notifies the channel, then awaits the event. The channel handler (HTTP endpoint or Telegram callback) sets the event. For HTTP: the SSE stream pauses while waiting; client sees the permission_request event and sends approval via REST. For Telegram: inline keyboard with approve/deny buttons. Use uuid4 for request_id. Important: the can_use_tool callback runs inside the SDK's event loop, so it must be async and non-blocking (just awaiting the Event is fine).
